extracted.intended_audience: shippers, carriers, manufacturers, package designers, radiation safety officers, and regulatory compliance staff involved in transport of radioactive materials (DOT/NRC regulated entities)
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register final rule amending the Hazardous Materials Regulations (49 CFR parts 171–178) to harmonize U.S. transport requirements for radioactive materials with IAEA TS-R-1 (1996/2000) and to add DOT-initiated requirements. Covers classification, packaging, marking, labeling, operational limits, and approval/certification procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nuclide-specific exemption activity concentrations and consignment activities (TS-R-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the TS-R-1 nuclide-specific exemption activity concentrations and nuclide-specific exemption consignment activities to define when material is regulated as Class 7 (radioactive). A material offered for transport is regulated as Class 7 only if both the activity concentration and the consignment activity are greater than the exemption values determined for that nuclide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemption values were selected to limit modeled annual worker doses to 0.01 mSv (1.0 mrem) across representative transport scenarios. Use both concentration and consignment thresholds (both must be exceeded to be regulated). Guidance and example mixture calculations may be obtained per §105.20. Gross alpha/beta counts may be insufficient to determine compliance; process knowledge or isotopic analyses may be necessary. For borderline batches, consider classifying material as LSA-I where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for certain naturally occurring radioactive materials (NORM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an exception so that certain naturally occurring radioactive materials are not subject to the HMR so long as their specific activities do not exceed 10 times the activity concentration exemption values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adopts the TS-R-1 exception for ores and natural materials not intended for their radioactive properties. The 10× threshold applies to specific activity relative to the tabulated exemption concentrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of TS-R-1 A1 and A2 values
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate the TS-R-1 changes in the A1 and A2 values into the HMR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A1/A2 values are used in determining package/type limits and transport classification (affects e.g., limits for excepted, Type A, and Type B packages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt new proper shipping names and UN identification numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the TS-R-1 new proper shipping names and UN identification numbers, except for entries referring to Type C packages, to fissile low specific activity (LSA) material, or to fissile surface contaminated objects (SCO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some previous DOT-specific shipping description requirements (e.g., mandatory inclusion of the words 'Radioactive Material') are removed when the proper shipping name already conveys that information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units formatting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If customary units are used, the appropriate customary unit quantity must be placed within parentheses positioned after the original quantity expressed in the International System of Units (SI units).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SI units are primary; customary units are optional but when used must follow SI in parentheses for consistency and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticality Safety Index (CSI) adoption and Transport Index (TI) restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the use of the Criticality Safety Index (CSI) (replacing the prior 'criticality control transport index'); restrict the use of the transport index (TI) to a number derived purely from the maximum radiation level at one meter from the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSI is used to control fissile material criticality safety during transport; TI is strictly a radiation-level-derived quantity (max dose at 1 m) and should not be used as a surrogate for criticality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fissile label and CSI marking requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Require the new fissile label be placed on each fissile material package and require that the CSI for that package be noted on the fissile label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling must reflect the package's CSI and use the standardized fissile label prescribed in the rule for international compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking requirements for excepted and industrial packagings
rubrics_metrics.description: Excepted packages must be marked with the UN identification number; industrial packagings must be marked with the package type; Type IP-2, IP-3 industrial packages and Type A packages must be marked with the international vehicle registration code of the country of origin of the packaging design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks are required on the outside of packages to identify UN numbers, package types, and country-of-origin design codes per international practice (improves traceability and conformity with TS-R-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of redundant shipping description requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove the former requirement that the shipping description contain the words 'Radioactive Material' when the proper shipping name already includes that information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamlines shipping descriptions by relying on harmonized proper shipping names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision to definition of fissile material (Pu-238 removal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove plutonium-238 (Pu-238) from the definition of fissile material and remove the reference to Pu-238 in the list of fissile radionuclides for which weight (g or kg) may be listed instead of or in addition to activity on shipping papers or radioactive labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes affect classification and reporting for shipments previously treated as fissile due to Pu-238.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of contamination and authorities for unpackaged LSA and SCO
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a definition of contamination and include an authority to transport unpackaged Low Specific Activity (LSA) material and Surface Contaminated Objects (SCO); authorize the use of qualified tank containers, freight containers and metal intermediate bulk containers (MIBCs) as industrial packagings (IP-2 and IP-3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides clarity on what constitutes contamination and allows additional container types to be used as industrial packagings when qualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: New LSA-I material classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a new class LSA-I consisting of radioactive material in which the activity is distributed throughout and the estimated average specific activity does not exceed 30 times the activity concentration exemption level; remove the prior category for mill tailings, contaminated earth, concrete, rubble, debris, and activated material with specific activity not exceeding 10^-6 A2/g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LSA-I classification offers relatively modest packaging and communication requirements compared to higher categories; it should be considered in borderline cases to reduce regulatory burden while maintaining safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: UF6 packaging technical requirements (>0.1 kg)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate TS-R-1 changes for packagings containing more than 0.1 kg of uranium hexafluoride (UF6): UF6 packagings must meet pressure, drop and thermal test requirements, prohibition on use of pressure relief devices, and certification in accordance with TS-R-1 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UF6 has special containment and accident characteristics; design/testing standards (pressure, drop, thermal) and prohibition on PRDs are mandated to ensure safety. ISO 7195 (1993) may be accepted as an alternative to ANSI N14.1 for certain requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and certification requirements for UF6 packagings (>0.1 kg)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each offeror of a package containing more than 0.1 kg of UF6 must maintain on file for at least one year after the latest shipment a complete safety analysis (including test documentation), provide it on request to the Associate Administrator, and obtain a U.S. Competent Authority Certificate prior to the first export shipment. Requests for competent authority certificates must include a safety analysis and, for original requests, evidence of a quality assurance program and a description of proposed pre-shipment actions; requests must be received at least 90 days before the requested effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IAEA Certificate of Competent Authority may be used to satisfy some requirements. Safety analysis must detail packaging/contents, manufacturing, tests/results, or calculative evidence of compliance with §173.420. This establishes administrative oversight and traceability for UF6 packaging designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-out and manufacture prohibition for legacy Type B specification packages (1967)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept IAEA transitional requirements and begin phase-out of packages satisfying the 1967 IAEA requirements (including DOT specification packages). Prohibit manufacture of all Type B specification packages conforming to Safety Series No. 6 (1967) as of the effective date, with use of existing packages allowed for three years after the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional provisions allow continued use for a limited period but stop new production of legacy-design Type B packages to harmonize with modern TS-R-1 standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for containment of active material in excepted instruments/articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Require that the active material in an instrument or article intended to be transported in an excepted package be completely enclosed by the non-active components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents release or exposure from small instruments/articles shipped under excepted package provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent Authority Certificate requirements for special form Class 7 materials
rubrics_metrics.description: For original requests for a Competent Authority Certificate for special form Class 7 material, provide evidence of a quality assurance program for design/manufacture/testing/documentation/use/maintenance/inspection as appropriate, and a description of any proposed pre-shipment actions (e.g., leak testing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QA program evidence and pre-shipment action descriptions are required to support competent authority approval of special form designs offered for transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rail transport TI and CSI limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit the number of packages of Class 7 material that may be transported by a rail car or stored at any single location by capping the total transport index (TI) and total criticality safety index (CSI) at not more than 50 each (provision does not apply to exclusive use shipments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls the collective radiation and criticality risk present in a single rail car or storage location. Fissile shipments must comply with applicable fissile material shipment requirements (§§173.457, 173.459).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fissile material shipments must meet CSI-based requirements (§§173.457/173.459)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each shipment of fissile material packages must conform to the requirements established in §§173.457 and 173.459, which base non-exclusive and exclusive use shipment controls on TS-R-1 package and conveyance CSI limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shipments of fissile material are managed by CSI limits, grouping and separation rules, and may require exclusive use or other mitigations under the cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passenger aircraft limits for Class 7 packages
rubrics_metrics.description: No person may transport in a passenger-carrying aircraft any package requiring RADIOACTIVE YELLOW-II, RADIOACTIVE YELLOW-III, or FISSILE labeling unless: (1) for Yellow-III, the TI does not exceed 3.0; (2) for FISSILE, the CSI does not exceed 3.0; (3) package is carried on the floor of the cargo compartment or in a freight container; (4) carried in accordance with §§175.701 and 175.703; (5) total sum of TIs aboard aircraft does not exceed 50; and (6) total sum of CSIs aboard aircraft does not exceed 50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple concurrent limits control suitability of passenger aircraft transport; TI/CSI caps and carriage location are specified to minimize passenger/crew exposure and risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cargo aircraft carriage limits and exclusive-use conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: For carriage in cargo aircraft: either (1) total TI ≤50 and total CSI ≤50 and carried per §175.701(a); or (2) total TI >50 but ≤200 and total CSI ≤100 with any package/overpack/consignment having CSI >50 transported under exclusive use and subject to group-level TI ≤50, group separation ≥6 m, and separation from spaces occupied by humans ≥9 m and live animals ≥0.5 m (≤24 h) or ≥1.0 m (>24 h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When larger consignments are carried, increased separation and exclusive-use measures are required; groups must be handled and stowed to meet TI and CSI group limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft acceptance and radiation limit controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Carriers may accept overpacked packages only if prepared for shipment per §172.403(h); shipments of fissile packages must conform to §§173.457/173.459; packages with surface radiation levels or TI exceeding §173.441(a) limits may not be transported by aircraft except under special arrangements approved by the Associate Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures acceptance procedures, conformance to fissile controls, and prohibition of high-radiation packages unless special approvals/arrangements are obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vessel freight container radiation limits and TI/CSI vessel limits (Table IIIA/IIIB)
rubrics_metrics.description: For freight containers on vessels: external radiation ≤2 mSv/h at any outside surface and ≤0.1 mSv/h at 2 m from outside surface; sum of TIs and CSIs for all packages on board must not exceed the limits in Table IIIA (TI) and Table IIIB (CSI). LSA-I consignments are excepted from some limits. Groups of fissile packages must be separated such that CSI group sums do not exceed specified limits (50 for non-exclusive, 100 for exclusive) and groups separated by at least 6 m. Under exclusive use, additional requirements (radiation protection program, pre-planned stowage, qualified supervision, and Associate Administrator approval) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables IIIA/IIIB specify numeric TI/CSI caps by freight container/conveyance type (e.g., small freight container or partial vessel areas). Exclusive-use shipments require flag-state competent authority demonstration and approval and operational controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segregation distances and crew/passenger dose criteria on vessels (Table IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Table IV to determine minimum separation distances between radioactive materials and spaces regularly occupied by crew or passengers (function of sum of TIs and intervening cargo); Category YELLOW-II or YELLOW-III packages must not be transported in spaces occupied by passengers (except authorized couriers). Alternatively, segregation distances for crew/passengers may be determined by direct measurement demonstrating dose rates below specified values: crew—7.0 μSv/h up to 700 h/yr or 1.8 μSv/h up to 2750 h/yr; passengers—1.8 μSv/h up to 550 h/yr. Any departure must be approved by competent authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table IV or measured dose demonstrations ensure crew and passenger exposure remain below stated operational limits. Intervening cargo density and interpolation may be used; flag-state competent authority approval required for departures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highway carriage fissile CSI limits and exclusive-use vehicle limits
rubrics_metrics.description: For public highway carriage of fissile Class 7 material: in non-exclusive use vehicles, sum of CSIs must not exceed 50; in loading/storage areas, groups must have CSI sums ≤50 and be separated by ≥6 m. For exclusive-use shipments, the radiation dose rate may not exceed 0.02 mSv/h in any position normally occupied in the motor vehicle, and the sum of CSIs for packages in the exclusive-use vehicle may not exceed 100.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls permit grouping and separation for non-exclusive shipments and stricter dose and CSI caps for exclusive-use highway shipments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification 7A (Type A) marking requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Specification 7A packaging must be marked on the outside 'USA DOT 7A Type A' and must comply with the marking requirements of §178.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized external marking ensures identification of Type A packagings and compliance with broader marking rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric TI and CSI table limits (Table IIIA and Table IIIB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish numeric limits for the total sum of transport indices (Table IIIA) and criticality safety indices (Table IIIB) for freight containers and conveyances (examples: not under exclusive use—small freight container/conveyance limit TI 50; vessel total TI 200; CSI limits similarly specified with values 50, 100, 200 etc depending on container/type and exclusive-use status).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Table IIIA and IIIB for precise numeric limits by conveyance/container type and exclusive-use status; these numeric caps govern allowable aggregated TI/CSI on conveyances and drive grouping/stowage decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of alternative standards for UF6 packaging (ISO 7195 acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorize the use of the 1993 edition of ISO 7195 as an alternative to ANSI N14.1 for UF6 packagings to meet required pressure, drop and thermal test requirements and certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits recognized international standard (ISO 7195:1993) as an alternative conformity path for UF6 packaging design and testing, facilitating international harmonization.
